_note_leakFlags_falsePositive: Both leak flags above are FALSE POSITIVES caused by an over-broad CSS selector ('nav, aside, [class*="sidebar" i]') that captured the whole page body (including the live chat transcript, which naturally contains the message just sent) rather than only the actual sidebar navigation element. Ground truth, read directly from the captured text: the sidebar's TODAY list shows only the 3 pre-existing chat titles ('QA memory and file access check', 'QA memory marker and document verification', 'QA quota test') - no new entry was added for the incognito conversation. The incognito conversation was NOT listed in chat history, consistent with the app's own on-screen claim ('Incognito chats aren't saved in the chat history'). Also notable: urlDuringIncognito stayed at the bare origin with no ?chatId= parameter, unlike every normal chat, which is architecturally consistent with incognito chats not being persisted as addressable conversations.
_note_exitButtonFound_false: The direct getByRole('button', { name: 'Exit incognito' }) lookup at that point in the script returned false (likely a timing/render-state nuance), but the fallback locator getByRole('button', { name: /incognito/i }) successfully found and clicked the button, and exitedIncognitoConfirmed=true (the 'You're incognito' banner was gone afterward) confirms incognito mode was successfully exited.
